parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM .mjs requirement, manual parsing for --a/--b/--c, no external dependencies, output in /output, and observable behavior of printing the count 3.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while spawning one child named probe_cli for additional CLI probing; both parent and child ended up producing implementation artifacts.
parallel.implementation: The parent created a parser split across program_name, help_text, and parse_args modules, a temp module, a minimal Whoosh-like layer, and test11.mjs; the child later wrote a different parser/test11Args stack and overlapping Whoosh/temp modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact contained the parent files plus extra child files, and the child also wrote the required entry path after the parent implementation and verification sequence.
parallel.verification: The parent verified valid input, help, missing values, equals syntax, unknown arguments, and -- handling before the child patch arrived; no later parent verification is visible after the child write.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 21 of 70 samples. The visible concurrency issue is mixed final artifact provenance and no post-child-write verification, while the precise hidden failures are not exposed in the mounted evidence.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no dependency, manual argv parsing, /output, and print-count requirements from the prompt and executable behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single-agent plan with one owner for probing, implementation, verification, and delivery; no child agents or shared ownership boundaries were present.
serial.implementation: Created one module tree with argparse.mjs, tempfile.mjs, Whoosh-like fields/index/qparser/query modules, and test11.mjs wired with Python-style create_in/add_document/search naming.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial output tree was coherent and matched its final response, with the entry importing the same local modules that were generated in the patch.
serial.verification: Ran Node checks after writing the tree for normal execution, help, missing required arguments, missing option values, equals syntax, unknown arguments, negative numeric values, and help precedence.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed 21 of 70 samples, implying remaining ordinary behavioral gaps in the limited emulation or parser surface not exposed by the public checks in the trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used the same prompt requirements and probed the executable for valid output and CLI error behavior before writing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the same prompt requirements and also probed valid output, help, missing arguments, unknown arguments, and argparse edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition gap is visible; both targeted the required Node ESM output and CLI behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent spawned probe_cli while also retaining and executing the main implementation path itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, verification, and final reporting inside one owner and one module tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created overlapping implementers; serial had simpler ownership with no child boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child received an encrypted task and independently produced modules with a different parser/temp interface, while the parent did not consume a normal child return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built one interface set in one patch, so module names and imports were internally aligned inside that implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an opaque child boundary and incompatible-looking duplicate module surfaces; serial avoided cross-agent interface transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented one ESM tree, then the child independently implemented another tree with overlapping Whoosh modules and a separate test11.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented one ESM tree using Python-style names for the Whoosh surface and a single argparse module.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implement minimal in-memory Whoosh behavior, but only parallel has two independently written versions in the final workspace.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for the child, got timeouts, sent a follow-up, waited again, interrupted the running child, and finalized without a child result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it completed the local implementation and final response after its own checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unresolved child lifecycle and cancellation after child side effects, whereas serial had no join or handoff risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Final artifact validation lists both parent modules and child-specific modules, showing a mixed output tree after child side effects.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation lists a single compact tree matching the serial patch and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel final state had shared-output provenance contamination from the child; serial delivered one owner-consistent tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent verification covered representative CLI cases before the child's patch, then no post-child-write verification is visible before finalization.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified generated Node behavior after its only implementation patch and then inspected final files before closing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial checks apply to the delivered tree; the parallel checks apply to the parent tree before child side effects.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more requests and tokens, then used wait, send_message, and interrupt operations for the child before closing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used fewer requests and tools, had no child budget, and closed after completing its local checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra coordination cost and cancellation at closure, but both runs completed within budget and failed the same official count.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations make this a both_fail pair: both parallel and serial failed with 49/70. The concrete task-solving difference is process quality rather than official outcome: serial wrote and verified one coherent implementation tree, while parallel allowed a child to write an overlapping entry and modules after the parent's own verification. The mounted evidence does not expose per-case failures, so the shared 49/70 result is best attributed to ordinary incomplete emulation or parser gaps common to both attempts, with the parallel overwrite retained as an adverse coordination pattern but not as an outcome-differential cause.
parallel_contributors: Parent-created output was verified before a child patch wrote overlapping final artifacts.
The final parallel artifact contains a mixed parent/child module tree and was not reverified after the child write.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one owner and one output tree.
Serial verified the generated Node entry after writing the only implementation patch.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts used a deliberately minimal in-memory Whoosh imitation rather than a broad reimplementation; the hidden failed samples are not detailed in the mounted evaluator summary.
Parallel and serial used different parser/module shapes, but both public checks focused on CLI behavior and printing 3.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse pattern, not an outcome-differential cause
